title: interp() performance regression in 2025.1.0+
body:
### What happened?

A performance regression has been introduced between 2024.11.0 and 2025.1.0, possibly in #9881, as was the case in #10287.  This issue is still present in 2025.8.0. In the example running on my machine it is a 76x performance regression. It seems to be present when interpolating 2D arrays but the degradation is more extreme with 3D arrays.

### What did you expect to happen?

No performance regression.

### Minimal Complete Verifiable Example

```Python
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

import time

n_repeats = 10

# array dims
n_t = 122
n_r = 65
n_z = 65

# generate some random data to interpolate
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)

data = rng.random((n_t, n_r, n_z))
data_t = np.linspace(0.01, 0.855, n_t)
data_r = np.linspace(0.04, 4., n_r)
data_z = np.linspace(-1.2, 1.2, n_z)

da = xr.DataArray(
    data=data,
    dims=["t", "r", "z"],
    coords=dict(
        t=data_t,
        r=data_r,
        z=data_z,
    ),
)

interp_z_data = rng.random((n_t))
interp_z = xr.DataArray(
    data=interp_z_data,
    dims=["t"],
    coords=dict(
        t=data_t,
    ),
)

start = time.time()
for _ in range(n_repeats):
    # regression is here:
    da.interp(z=interp_z)
end = time.time()

t_elapsed = end - start
print(f"Time elapsed: {t_elapsed}")
```

### MVCE confirmation

- [x] Minimal example — the example is as focused as reasonably possible to demonstrate the underlying issue in xarray.
- [x] Complete example — the example is self-contained, including all data and the text of any traceback.
- [x] Verifiable example — the example copy & pastes into an IPython prompt or [Binder notebook](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/pydata/xarray/main?urlpath=lab/tree/doc/examples/blank_template.ipynb), returning the result.
- [x] New issue — a search of GitHub Issues suggests this is not a duplicate.
- [x] Recent environment — the issue occurs with the latest version of xarray and its dependencies.

### Relevant log output

```Python
pip install "xarray==2024.11.0"
python test.py
Time elapsed: 0.22251605987548828

pip install "xarray==2025.1.0"
python test.py
Time elapsed: 16.765803813934326
```

comments.author: ianhi
comments.text: I looked into this a little bit, and it seems as though the vectorization is breaking down in this case with the ufunc applying interpnd( https://github.com/pydata/xarray/blob/5d9aa6e22955ed49d52659667adfe7abec6848b6/xarray/core/missing.py#L786) 7930 per run ( 7930 = 122 *65) which ends up taking up more than 70% of the runtime my first guess (need to investigate more) is that this is happening due to some negative consequence of `interp_z` varying along the `t` dimension which is where we are getting our 122 x 65 from

comments.author: leroyvn
comments.text:
Hi, I am running into this issue once more. [One of my libraries](https://github.com/eradiate/axsdb/) breaks down multivariate interpolation into a sequence of univariate interpolations to adjust the out-of-bound error handling policy depending on the processed dimension. I've recently upgraded xarray in my dev environment from 2024.11 to 2026.1 and saw a huge performance hit that makes this approach completely impractical. Here is a MWE:
mwe.py ```python """ Minimal Working Example for xarray interpolation bug report. This script demonstrates an issue with multi-dimensional interpolation in xarray where using `interp()` with all dimensions at once vs. sequential interpolation produces different behaviour. """ import argparse import numpy as np import xarray as xr # Create synthetic thermoprops dataset (atmospheric profile with 121 altitude levels) z_levels = 121 thermoprops = xr.Dataset( { "t": ("z", np.linspace(187, 360, z_levels)), # Temperature (K) "p": ("z", np.logspace(np.log10(2.54e-3), np.log10(1.013e5), z_levels)), # Pressure (Pa) "x_H2O": ("z", np.logspace(np.log10(2.0e-7), np.log10(7.75e-3), z_levels)), # H2O mixing ratio "x_O3": ("z", np.logspace(np.log10(5.0e-10), np.log10(7.84e-6), z_levels)), # O3 mixing ratio "x_CO2": ("z", np.linspace(3.5e-5, 3.3e-4, z_levels)), # CO2 mixing ratio }, coords={"z": np.linspace(0, 120, z_levels)}, # Altitude (km) ) # Create synthetic sigma_a data array (absorption coefficient from CKD database) # Dimensions: (x_CO2, x_H2O, x_O3, p, t, g) # This mimics the structure from a correlated k-distribution absorption database da = xr.DataArray( np.random.rand(2, 4, 2, 16, 8, 32), # Random absorption coefficients dims=["x_CO2", "x_H2O", "x_O3", "p", "t", "g"], coords={ "x_CO2": [0.0, 5.0e-4], "x_H2O": [0.0, 1.0e-6, 1.0e-5, 1.0e-4], "x_O3": [0.0, 1.0e-5], "p": np.logspace(2, 5, 16), # 100 to 100,000 Pa "t": np.linspace(200, 340, 8), # 200 to 340 K "g": np.linspace(0, 1, 32), # g-points for quadrature }, ) # Build interpolation coordinate list # Note: Only species present in da.dims are included species_dims = ["x_H2O", "x_O3", "x_CO2"] dims_coords = [ ("g", [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]), ("t", thermoprops["t"]), ("p", thermoprops["p"]), *[ (species_dim, thermoprops[species_dim]) for species_dim in species_dims ], ] def interp_multi(da, dims_coords, interp_kwargs: dict | None = None): print(f"{da.shape = }") if interp_kwargs is None: interp_kwargs = {} da = da.interp(dict(dims_coords), **interp_kwargs) print(f"{da.shape = }") return da def interp_seq(da, dims_coords, interp_kwargs: dict | None = None): if interp_kwargs is None: interp_kwargs = {} print(f"{da.shape = }") for dim, coords in dims_coords: if dim in da.dims: da = da.interp({dim: coords}, **interp_kwargs) print(f"{dim}: {da.shape = }") return da interp_kwargs = { "method": "linear", "assume_sorted": True, "kwargs": {"bounds_error": False, "fill_value": None}, } def cli(mode): print(f"{mode = }") if mode == "multi": interp_multi(da, dims_coords, interp_kwargs=interp_kwargs) elif mode == "seq": interp_seq(da, dims_coords, interp_kwargs=interp_kwargs) else: raise ValueError(mode) if __name__ == "__main__": parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("mode", help="Interpolation mode: 'multi' or 'seq'") args = parser.parse_args() cli(args.mode) ```
Timings look like this (averaged over 10 runs; all using Python 3.12, numpy 2.2.3 and scipy 1.15.2 on macOS): Mode | 2024.11 | 2026.1 ------- | ------- | ------ `multi` | 0.8s | 0.9s `seq` | 0.8s | 4.0s Is there an alternative other than reimplementing something like the 2024.11 algorithm myself?

comments.author: ianhi
comments.text: I remember from looking into this that in https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/9881#discussion_r1883377901 there is a a possibilty of adding another path to that function that would allow for catchigni this slowed down case. PRs welcome if you can parse out the correct logic to add back a happy path for this case.

comments.author: dcherian
comments.text: I spent a while on the "proper" solution and it was quite hard (we basically have to dump apply_ufunc and rewrite a bunch of it; or find some clever way to stitch together apply_ufunc's primitives). I support adding a workaround that is triggered when `.chunks is None`

comments.author: leroyvn
comments.text: for what it's worth, I wrote [some workaround code](https://github.com/eradiate/axsdb/blob/36dd43667dff0e710b92bea7409b0d41e4008f83/src/axsdb/interpolation.py) that mixes calls to a custom Numba gufunc and Scipy's `interpn()` function. The performance of that approach compares to what xarray's `interp()` achieves (actually a bit better), but it's tailored to my use case so I'm not sure how relevant that would be to solve the general issue.
